forecast-period.text: A cold front and trough will track east today clearing South Australia as a ridge of high pressure develops in its wake. A trough is then expected to develop near the western border on Sunday and remain near stationary nearly next week.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Isolated showers and thunderstorms about the Flinders and North East Pastoral districts, contracting east and clearing during the morning. Gusty showers and thunderstorms about the southern agricultural area, contracting to the southeast during the afternoon. Thunderstorms may be severe about the Lower South East with the risk of damaging wind gusts. Maximum temperatures below average, tending above average in the far northeast. Fresh to strong and gusty west to northwesterly winds across the south, contracting to the southeast during the afternoon. Winds turning south to southwesterly during the day and remaining fresh at times.

Patchy morning fog about the Eyre Peninsula, Mid North and Flinders districts. Isolated light showers about southern coastal districts. Isolated showers and thunderstorms developing in the far west in the afternoon and evening. Maximum temperatures near to below average. Southeast to southwesterly winds, tending northeasterly in the west.

Isolated light showers possible about the southeast coasts during the morning, with isolated showers and possible thunderstorms continuing in the west. Maximum temperatures near to below average. Southeast to southwesterly winds, fresh and gusty about northern parts during the day.

text.p: Morning fog and possible frost in the southeast. Dry, apart from isolated showers and possible thunderstorms in the west. Maximum temperatures near to below average. Southeast to southwesterly winds, fresh at times near the west coast.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Tuesday: Dry in the northeast. Elsewhere, 1 to 5 mm, increasing to 5 to 10 mm in the far west, northwest and the southeast with isolated falls of 10 to 15mm, possibility reaching 25 mm in the west.
